title.full: Using agency names in healthcare ads

summary.text: HCSA does not control these names. The relevant agencies do, and ads must be factual and not misleading.

details.heading: Who controls the names
details.body: HCSA does not govern the use of names of MOH’s related agencies in advertising. The agencies whose programs the services claim to be part of control their use. Licensees must follow the rules for those programs.

details.heading: What the advertisements must do
details.body: Advertisements should be factual and not misleading to the general public. They must also comply with the Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations.

example_phrasings: Can healthcare ads use MOH agency names?
May a clinic say it is part of Healthier SG?
Are names like HSA programs allowed in ads?
Are there provisions to prevent a licensee from using names of MOH's related agencies in their advertisement?

sources.page_title: Are there provisions to prevent a licensee from using names of MOH's related agencies in their advertisement? For example, can licensees use terms like “MOH’s Healthier SG” or "HSA's XXXX Program" when advertising their healthcare services?

quotes.text: HCSA does not govern the use of names of MOH’s related agencies in advertising.
However, this will be controlled by the agencies whose programs the services purport to be a part of. Licensees will need to comply with the rules stipulated for the respective programs.

In general, licensees should ensure that their advertisements are factual and not deemed to be misleading to the general public and comply with all the requirements under Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations.
